source_text: Περιπατοῦντός μου εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν καὶ κατανοοῦντος πτελέαν καὶ ἄμπελον καὶ διακρίνοντος περὶ αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν, φανεροῦταί μοι ὁ ποιμὴν καὶ λέγει: Τί σὺ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ζητεῖς περὶ τῆς πτελέας καὶ τῆς ἀμπέλου; Συζητῶ, φημί, κύριε, ὅτι εὐπρεπέσταταί εἰσιν ἀλλήλαις. Ταῦτα τὰ δύο δένδρα, φησίν, εἰς τύπον κεῖνται τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ. Ἤθελον, φημί, γνῶναι τὸν τύπον τῶν δένδρων τούτων ὧν λέγεις. Βλέπεις, φησί, τὴν πτελέαν καὶ τὴν ἄμπελον; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε. Ἡ ἄμπελος, φησίν, αὕτη καρπὸν φέρει, ἡ δὲ πτελέα ξύλον ἄκαρπόν ἐστιν: ἀλλ’ ἡ ἄμπελος αὕτη ἐὰν μὴ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν πτελέαν, οὐ δύναται καρποφορῆσαι πολὺ ἐρριμμένη χαμαί, καὶ ὃν φέρει καρπόν, σεσηπότα φέρει μὴ κρεμαμένη ἐπὶ τῆς πτελέας, ὅταν οὖν ἐπιρριφῇ ἡ ἄμπελος ἐπὶ τὴν πτελέαν, καὶ παῤ ἑαυτῆς φέρει καρπὸν καὶ παρὰ τῆς πτελέας. βλέπεις οὖν, ὅτι καὶ ἡ πτελέα πολὺν καρπὸν δίδωσιν, οὐκ ἐλάσσονα τῆς ἀμπέλου, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ πλείονα. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, πλείονα; Ὅτι, φησίν, ἡ ἄμπελος κρεμαμένη ἐπὶ τὴν πτελέαν τὸν καρπὸν πολὺν καὶ καλὸν δίδωσιν, ἐρριμμένη δὲ χαμαὶ ὀλίγον καὶ σαπρὸν φέρει. αὕτη οὖν ἡ παραβολὴ εἰς τοὺς δούλους τοῦ θεοῦ κεῖται, εἰς πτωχὸν καὶ πλούσιον. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, γνώρισον μοι. Ἄκουε, φησίν: ὁ μὲν πλούσιος ἔχει χρήματα, τὰ δὲ πρὸς τὸν κύριον πτωχεύει, περισπώμενος περὶ τὸν πλοῦτον ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ λίαν μικρὰν ἔχει τὴν ἔντευξιν καὶ τὴν ἐξομολόγησιν πρὸς τὸν κύριον, καὶ ἣν ἔχει, βληχρὰν καὶ μικρὰν καὶ ἄλλην μὴ ἔχουσαν δύναμιν. ὅταν οὖν ἐπαναπάῃ ἐπὶ τὸν πένητα ὁ πλούσιος καὶ χορηγήσῃ αὐτῷ τὰ δέοντα, πιστεύει, ὅτι ἐὰν ἐργάσηται εἰς τὸν πένητα δυνηθήσεται τὸν μισθὸν εὑρεῖν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ: ὅτι ὁ πένης πλούσιός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ ἐντεύξει καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐξομολογήσει καὶ δύναμιν μεγάλην ἔχει παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἡ ἔντευξις αὐτοῦ. ἐπιχορηγεῖ οὖν ὁ πλούσιος τῷ πένητι πάντα ἀδιστάκτως. ὁ πένης δὲ ἐπιχορηγούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ πλουσίου ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ, ὑπὲρ τοῦ διδόντος αὐτῷ: κἀκεῖνος ἔτι ἐπισπουδάζει περὶ τοῦ πένητος, ἵνα ἀδιάλειπτος γένηται ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ: οἶδε γάρ, ὅτι ἡ τοῦ πένητος ἔντευξις προσδεκτή ἐστι καὶ πλουσία πρὸς κύριον. ἀμφότεροι οὖν τὸ ἔργον τελοῦσιν: ὁ μὲν πένης ἐργάζεται τῇ ἐντεύξει, ἐν ᾗ πλουτεῖ, ἣν ἔλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου: ταύτην ἀποδίδωσι τῷ κυρίῳ τῷ ἐπιχορηγοῦντι αὐτῷ. καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ὡσαύτως τὸ πλοῦτος, ὃ ἔλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ἀδιστάκτως παρέχεται τῷ πένητι. καὶ τοῦτο ἔργον μέγα ἐστὶ καὶ δεκτὸν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ, ὅτι συνῆκεν ἐπὶ τῷ πλούτῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰργάσατο εἰς τὸν πένητα ἐκ τῶν δωρημάτων τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἐτέλεσε τὴν διακονίαν ὀρθῶς. παρὰ τοῖς οὖν ἀνθρώποις ἡ πτελέα δοκεῖ καρπὸν μὴ φέρειν, καὶ οὐκ οἴδασιν οὐδὲ νοοῦσιν, ὅτι, ὅταν ἀβροχία γένηται, ἡ πτελέα ἔχουσα ὕδωρ τρέφει τὴν ἄμπελον καὶ ἡ ἄμπελος ἀδιάλειπτον ἔχουσα τὸ ὕδωρ διπλοῦν τὸν καρπὸν ἀποδίδωσι, καὶ ὑπὲρ ἑαυτῆς καὶ ὑπὲρ τῆς πτελέας. οὕτως καὶ οἱ πένητες ὑπὲρ τῶν πλουσίων ἐντυγχάνοντες πρὸς τὸν κύριον πληροφοροῦσι τὸ πλοῦτος αὐτῶν, καὶ πάλιν οἱ πλούσιοι χορηγοῦντες τοῖς πένησι τὰ δέοντα πληροφοροῦσι τὰς εὐχὰς αὐτῶν. γίνονται οὖν ἀμφότεροι κοινωνοὶ τοῦ ἔργου τοῦ δικαίου. ταῦτα οὖν ὁ ποιῶν οὐκ ἐγκαταλειφθήσεται ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἔσται γεγραμμένος εἰς τὰς βίβλους τῶν ζώντων. μακάριοι οἱ ἔχοντες καὶ συνιέντες, ὅτι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου πλουτίζονται, ὁ γὰρ συνίων τοῦτο δυνήσεται καὶ διακονῆσαί τι ἀγαθόν.
pass_a_gloss: As I was walking in the field and considering the elm and the vine and discerning about them and their fruits, the Shepherd appears to me and says: What are you seeking within yourself about the elm and the vine? I am discussing, I say, Lord, because they are very suitable for each other. These two trees, he says, are set as a type for the servants of God. I want, I say, to know the type of these trees which you speak of. Do you see, he says, the elm and the vine? I see, I say, Lord. The vine, he says, bears fruit, but the elm is a barren tree: however, this vine, if it does not climb up onto the elm, is not able to bear much fruit, thrown down on the ground, and the fruit it bears is rotten, not hanging from the elm; when, therefore, the vine is thrown upon the elm and bears fruit from itself and from the elm. Do you see, then, that the elm also gives much fruit, not less than the vine, but even more? How, I say, Lord, more? Because, he says, the vine hanging from the elm gives much and good fruit, but thrown down on the ground, it bears little and rotten fruit. This parable, then, is set for the servants of God, for the poor and the rich. How, I say, Lord, make it known to me. Listen, he says: the rich man has money, but he is poor in relation to the Lord, being distracted by his own wealth, and he has very little prayer and confession to the Lord, and what he has is weak and small and without power. When, therefore, the rich man goes up to the poor man and provides for him what he needs, he believes that if he works for the poor man, he will be able to find his reward from God: because the poor man is rich in prayer and confession and has great power with God, his prayer. The rich man, then, provides for the poor man all things without hesitation. The poor man, being provided for by the rich man, prays to God, giving thanks to him on behalf of the one giving to him: and the rich man still takes care of the poor man, so that he may be uninterrupted in his life: for he knows that the poor man's prayer is acceptable and rich to the Lord. Both, then, complete the work: the poor man works with his prayer, in which he is rich, which he received from the Lord: he gives this back to the Lord who provides for him. And the rich man, in the same way, gives his wealth, which he received from the Lord, without hesitation to the poor man. And this is a great and acceptable work to God, because he used his wealth and worked for the poor man from the Lord's gifts and completed the ministry correctly. Among men, then, the elm seems not to bear fruit, and they do not know or understand that, when there is a drought, the elm, having water, nourishes the vine, and the vine, having uninterrupted water, gives double fruit, both for itself and for the elm. So also the poor, praying on behalf of the rich to the Lord, fulfill their wealth, and again the rich, providing for the poor what they need, fulfill their prayers. They become, then, both sharers of the work of righteousness. The one doing these things, then, will not be abandoned by God, but will be written in the books of the living. Blessed are those who have and understand that they are enriched by the Lord, for the one understanding this will be able to serve something good.
pass_b_english: I was walking through the field, looking at an elm and a vine and thinking about them and their fruit, when the Shepherd appeared to me. He asked, "What are you debating within yourself about the elm and the vine?" I replied, "Lord, I am discussing it because they are remarkably suited to each other." He said, "These two trees are set as a pattern for the servants of God." I told him, "Lord, I want to understand the pattern of these trees you speak of." He asked, "Do you see the elm and the vine?" I answered, "Yes, Lord, I see them." He explained, "This vine bears fruit, but the elm is a barren tree. However, if this vine does not climb up onto the elm, it cannot bear much fruit lying thrown on the ground, and whatever fruit it does produce is rotten because it is not suspended on the elm. But when the vine is thrown upon the elm, it bears fruit both from itself and from the elm. So do you see that the elm also yields a great deal of fruit, not less than the vine, but actually more?" I asked, "How can it be more, Lord?" He said, "Because the vine hanging on the elm produces abundant good fruit, but thrown on the ground it yields only a little rotten fruit."

He continued, "This parable is set for the servants of God, for the poor and the rich." I said, "Lord, make it known to me." He said, "Listen. The rich man has money, but he is poor toward the Lord, distracted by his own wealth. He has very little prayer and confession to the Lord, and what he does have is feeble, small, and lacks power. But when the rich man approaches the poor man and supplies what he needs, he believes that by working for the poor man he will find his reward from God. For the poor man is rich in prayer and confession, and his prayer has great power with God. The rich man therefore supplies the poor man with everything without hesitation. The poor man, being supplied by the rich man, prays to God, giving thanks on behalf of the one who gave to him. And the rich man keeps caring for the poor man so that his life may continue uninterrupted, because he knows that the poor man's prayer is acceptable and rich toward the Lord. Both, then, complete the work. The poor man works by means of the prayer in which he is rich, which he received from the Lord; he gives this back to the Lord who supplies him. And the rich man, in the same way, provides the wealth he received from the Lord to the poor man without hesitation. This is a great and acceptable work before God, because he made good use of his wealth and labored for the poor man from the Lord's gifts and carried out the ministry correctly."

He added, "Among people, the elm appears not to bear fruit, and they do not know or understand that when drought comes, the elm, having water, sustains the vine, and the vine, having uninterrupted water, yields double fruit — both for itself and for the elm. So also the poor, interceding for the rich before the Lord, fill up their wealth, and again the rich, supplying the poor with what they need, fill up their prayers. They become, then, both partners in the work of righteousness. The one who does these things will not be abandoned by God, but will be written in the books of the living. Blessed are those who possess and understand, because they are enriched by the Lord; for the one who understands this will be able to serve something good."

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the dialogue and the theological nuances of the Greek text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and specific nuances (e.g., 'without hesitation' for 'ἀδιστάκτως'), and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that remains faithful to the source. The distinction between the rich man's wealth and his poverty toward the Lord is correctly maintained. All scripture-alluded concepts (books of the living) are handled correctly.
